manual.title: How to talk to Chapeaux Fous
manual.introduction: Name a hat when you want to make the destination or role explicit. When the request is already clear, speak naturally and skip the hat.
manual.destinationRule: A hat identifies the role or destination for the relevant part of the request. It does not prevent Chapeaux Fous from using other tools needed to finish the work.
manual.multipleRule: Use more than one hat in the same request when the work crosses roles. Chapeaux Fous follows explicitly spoken hats in the order they appear.

hats.label: email
hats.description: Read, draft, send, organize, and clean up email.
hats.example: Chapeaux Fous, as my email, send John the invoice.

hats.label: contacts
hats.description: Find, create, import, tag, and merge contacts.
hats.example: Chapeaux Fous, as my contacts, find Tim's phone number.

hats.label: to-do
hats.description: Manage the personal to-do list and its groups.
hats.example: Chapeaux Fous, as my to-do, add a task to replace the furnace filter.

hats.label: log
hats.description: Record and review grouped personal logs and trackers.
hats.example: Chapeaux Fous, as my log, record that I weigh 180 pounds today.

hats.label: calendar
hats.description: Read and manage calendar events and schedules.
hats.example: Chapeaux Fous, as my calendar, add a dentist appointment Tuesday at 14:00.

hats.label: property manager
hats.description: Work with properties, buildings, projects, and property tasks.
hats.example: Chapeaux Fous, as my property manager, add a roof inspection task.

hats.label: weatherman
hats.description: Look up locations, forecasts, and weather conditions.
hats.example: Chapeaux Fous, as my weatherman, will it freeze tonight?
